Wanting more from your life and having no idea where to start is a lonely place to sit.

The first step can be small enough to feel a little silly. One page. One drawer cleaned out. One walk without the phone.

Small and a little silly is still moving.

hits.full_text:
This is a life-changing stress hack:

- Double-inhale through the nose
- Slow exhale through the mouth
- Repeat 3x

Do it before a big presentation or anytime you feel your stress levels rising. Immediate stress reduction. Almost too good to be true.

Highly recommend. https://t.co/m0EZOHixbX
hits.hook: SahilBloom: double inhale, slow exhale, 3x before stress (how-to with bullets)
hits.draft_en:
Two short breaths in through the nose, one long breath out. Three rounds.

I'm trying it before I open the notebook on mornings I'd rather not. It won't fix the day. It might get me to the first line, and most days that's the hard part.

Then open the notebook and write the first line of the day. No text on screen until the last two seconds: 'First line.'

reply_ideas.reply_text: What I keep relearning is to make the first move smaller than feels respectable. One page, one walk, one email I've been avoiding. The gap between where I am and "more" gets a lot quieter once something is moving.
I don't think most people sitting in that feeling are lazy. They just can't see a first step small enough to take today. Finding that step is most of the work.
The slow exhale is the part I'd rush, so I'm going to count it out. Three rounds before I open my notebook tomorrow morning. Fifteen seconds and nothing to buy, which I appreciate.
Saving this for [the thing you're dreading this week]. I like advice that fits in the time it takes the kettle to boil.
